answer: The bridge test I would run is Bridge transaction history over two years: crossings spread over two years, not one day, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm that reuses one proof across ten accounts is caught at the second account, because crossings spread over two years, not one day is bound to a single identity — the ivory is that reuse itself becomes the evidence. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the fable of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
